diagnostic_evidence.quote: For every $\delta \in [\delta_{\mathrm{th}}(\eta), \overline\delta)$ and every $x \in \RR^2$ with $I(\delta;\,x) = 0$, equality holds in Axiom~\ref{cond:monotonicity} if and only if $\nabla \risk(x) = 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: Axiom (A6) is quantified over the closed interval $[\delta_{\mathrm{th}}(\eta), \overline\delta)$. At the endpoint $\delta = \eta = \delta_{\mathrm{th}}$, the scalar remainder vanishes identically, $R^\sca(\eta;x) = \eta(\eta-\eta)(\eta^2-4)L^2 = 0$, so $I(\eta;\gd_\eta(x)) = I(\eta;x) = 0$ holds at EVERY point of the level set $\{\isc(\eta;\cdot)=0\}$, including non-stationary points (e.g. $\eta=1/2$, $(a,b)=(2,(1+\sqrt{15})/2)$ lies on $\isc(1/2;\cdot)=0$ with $ab\neq1$). Hence (A6) fails at $\delta=\eta$ for $\isc$; likewise $R^\fac(\eta) = -\eta^4 u^2v^2$ vanishes on non-stationary level-set points with $uv=0$, so (A6) fails at the endpoint for $\ifac$ and $\iapx$ as well. Stationarity holds only for $\delta \in (\eta, 2)$.

failure_location.quote: One verifies directly that Axioms~\ref{cond:P_is_pd}--\ref{cond:symmetry} hold with $\delta_{\mathrm{th}}(\eta) = \eta$ when $\eta <2$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Amend the remark to state that Axioms (A1)--(A5) and (A7) hold with $\delta_{\mathrm{th}}(\eta)=\eta$ while stationarity (A6) holds for $\delta \in (\eta, 2)$ (the endpoint being measure-zero for the certified-region applications), or equivalently verify the axioms on the open interval.
issues.overall_effect: The unnumbered remark's claim that Axioms (A1)--(A7) hold with $\delta_{\mathrm{th}}(\eta)=\eta$ is false as stated at the endpoint. No theorem loses content: the convergence applications of the abstract framework only invoke stationarity at $\delta_t > \eta$, and almost every certified initialization satisfies $\delta_0 > \eta$ strictly (the certified boundary $\{\ifac(\eta\sigma;\tilde x_0)=0\}$ has measure zero), so thm:abstract_state_dependent_convergence and its applications to the concrete certificates are unaffected.
issues.title: Stationarity axiom fails at the threshold endpoint delta = eta for the concrete certificates
issues.why_classification: The false claim is confined to one sentence of an unnumbered remark; the endpoint failure is a measure-zero degeneracy for every application of the framework (a.e. certified trajectories have $\delta_t>\eta$), and the repair is a one-line local restriction of the stationarity interval that preserves all theorems, rates, and scope.

For $\sigma>0$, the detected pass region is non-empty only above a $\sigma$-dependent lower threshold in $\delta$, reminiscent of the $q_\eta(\delta)<0$ threshold in the rank-1 approximation analysis.

issues.failure_explanation: The caption of the $\eta=0.6$ pass/fail heatmap (fig:xi_delta_heatmap2) asserts the pass region is non-empty for every sampled $\delta \in [0.05,1.95]$ in every panel, while the results text (ii) of the same appendix states that at $\eta=0.6$ the pass region is empty below a $\sigma$-dependent lower threshold in $\delta$. Both cannot be true; the $\eta=0.6$ caption repeats verbatim the sentence from the $\eta=0.2$ caption (fig:xi_delta_heatmap), which is consistent with results text (i), indicating the $\eta=0.6$ caption is the misreport.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Amend the caption of fig:xi_delta_heatmap2 so it agrees with the results text (pass region empty below the empirical threshold at $\eta=0.6$), or, if the scan in fact shows non-emptiness for all sampled $\delta$, correct the results text instead; one of the two statements must be changed so the source is internally consistent.
issues.overall_effect: The paper contradicts itself about its own numerical evidence for the admissible branch $\xi(\delta)$ at $\eta=0.6$: either the caption or the results text misreports the scan. The main-text narrative and the theory (the $q_\eta(\delta)<0$ threshold) agree with the results text, so the caption is the unreliable statement. No formal theorem or proved guarantee is affected.
issues.title: The eta = 0.6 heatmap caption contradicts the reported threshold behavior
issues.why_classification: The defect is an internal inconsistency in the reporting of numerical experiments in an appendix; it involves no proved statement, and the surrounding theory and main text identify which side is correct. Correcting one sentence (caption or results text) is a local edit with no loss of mathematical content.
